brief:
PROD-1422 — Tighten POST /api/uploads validation

We currently accept any file on POST /api/uploads, which has led to a couple of incidents (16MB jpegs from camera apps, .exe files renamed to .png). Add validation to the existing route:

- Accept only these MIME types: `image/jpeg`, `image/png`, `image/webp`. Anything else → 415 `{ error: 'unsupported_type' }`.
- Reject files larger than 5 MB → 413 `{ error: 'file_too_large' }`.
- Reject if `filename` is missing or contains path separators (`/` or `\`) → 400 `{ error: 'invalid_filename' }`.
- The handler currently just echoes the metadata; keep that behaviour after validation passes.

Don't add new dependencies — use Express's body parser only.
acceptance_criteria: MIME types outside the allowlist return 415 unsupported_type
Missing or path-traversal filenames return 400 invalid_filename
Valid uploads echo metadata as before (200)

hidden_tests.name: validation

seeded_mistakes.bug_description: Compass may check size before MIME, leaking a 413 message for an .exe upload that's also large.
seeded_mistakes.why_compass_might_suggest_it: Order rarely matters... until it does (info leak).

seeded_mistakes.bug_description: Compass may use `path.basename()` to sanitize instead of rejecting outright, letting `..%2F..%2Fetc%2Fpasswd` slip through if a parser ever URL-decodes.

rubric_anchors.check: All three rejection paths return the right status + error key
Filename rejected (not sanitised); MIME allowlist not blocklist — exercises traversal + boundary cases
Constants extracted, helper for filename validation

good_prompts_look_like: Should I allowlist or blocklist MIME types?
What's the right status code for too-large vs wrong-type?
Sanitize the filename or reject it outright?
common_verification_traps: Forgetting to test the path-traversal filename case
Not testing exactly at the 5MB boundary

interview_parallel: Razorpay / Cleartrip backend take-home — file upload validation comes up in nearly every 'add this feature' round.
